en: Year of the Dragon; person born in a Dragon year

examples.ko: 제 동생은 용띠이고 저는 토끼띠라서 한 살 차이예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a Dragon and I am a Rabbit, so we are one year apart.
My father is a Dragon and my mother is a Snake.
Are you a Dragon, Minsu? We are the same age, then.

examples.ko: 용띠 해에 태어난 사람은 성격이 어때요?
examples.en: What are people born in the year of the dragon like?
My friend who is a Dragon said tomorrow is their birthday.
I am not a Dragon, I am a Tiger.

explain: 나이를 직접 묻기 조심스러울 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물어요. 같은 띠는 열두 해마다 돌아와서, 띠를 알면 대략 나이를 짐작할 수 있어요. '용띠 해', '용띠 생'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: When it feels rude to ask someone's age directly, people ask '무슨 띠예요?' (What's your zodiac animal?). The same animal returns every twelve years, so knowing it lets you guess the age. You also hear '용띠 해' (year of the dragon).

examples.ko: 아기가 우유병을 두 손으로 꼭 잡고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is holding the milk bottle tightly with both hands.
This milk bottle is light and easy to wash.
I mixed formula in the bottle and gave it to the baby.

examples.ko: 동생이 이제 우유병 대신 컵으로 마셔요.
examples.en: My little brother now drinks from a cup instead of a milk bottle.
I don't know where the milk bottle went.
The baby drinks milk slowly from the bottle.

explain: 아기에게 우유를 먹이는 병을 말해요. 실제로는 '젖병'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 소독하다, 씻다, 타다 같은 말과 같이 많이 나와요.
explain_en: This is the bottle used to feed a baby. In real life people more often say '젖병'. It often appears with verbs like 소독하다 (sterilize), 씻다 (wash) and 타다 (mix).

examples.en: The baby's skin is milky white, so it's really pretty.

examples.ko: 아침 안개 속에서 호수가 우윳빛으로 보였어요.
examples.en: In the morning fog the lake looked milky white.
I bought a milky white ceramic cup.
That actor is famous for milky white skin.
The winter morning sky is hazy, like milk.
This paint is a white close to milky white.

explain: 순백이 아니라 약간 부드럽고 탁한 흰색을 말할 때 써요. 피부를 칭찬할 때 '우윳빛 피부'라고 많이 해요. '분홍빛'처럼 '빛'이 붙는 색 표현 중 하나예요.
explain_en: It describes a soft, slightly opaque white rather than pure white. People often praise skin as '우윳빛 피부'. It is one of the '-빛' color words, like '분홍빛'.

examples.en: The mailman brings letters every morning.
I greeted the mailman.
When I was little, my dream was to be a mailman.
Mail carriers work even on rainy days.
I handed the package to the mailman.
I rode my bike around the neighborhood like a mail carrier.

explain: 편지와 소포를 배달하는 사람을 말해요. 직업을 가리키는 말로는 '집배원'도 많이 써요. 친근하게 부를 때는 '집배원 아저씨'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the person who delivers letters and parcels. '집배원' is also widely used as the job title. When addressing them in a friendly way, people say '집배원 아저씨'.

examples.en: You have to renew your driver's license before it expires.

examples.ko: 운전면허증을 집에 두고 와서 렌터카를 못 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I left my driver's license at home, so I couldn't rent a car.
I don't like the photo on my driver's license.

examples.ko: 신분증 대신 운전면허증으로도 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also verify with a driver's license instead of an ID card.
I don't have a driver's license, so I take the bus.
The address on my driver's license is still the old one.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '면허증'이나 '면허'라고 많이 말해요. '면허를 따다'(취득하다), '면허를 갱신하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사를 알아 두세요. 신분증 대신 내밀 수 있는 카드이기도 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk people shorten it to '면허증' or '면허'. Learn the common verbs, such as '면허를 따다' (get a license) and '면허를 갱신하다' (renew it). It can also serve as an ID card.

examples.ko: 원두커피 전문점이 우리 동네에 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new coffee shop specializing in brewed coffee opened in our neighborhood.
I brew my own coffee from beans every morning.
Brewed coffee has a stronger aroma than instant mix coffee.

examples.ko: 이 원두커피로 아이스 아메리카노를 만들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please make an iced Americano with this coffee.
How much is one cup of brewed coffee?
At the office I drink brewed coffee with milk in it.

explain: '믹스커피', '인스턴트커피'와 대비해서 원두를 갈아 내린 커피를 말해요. 카페에서 파는 커피는 보통 원두커피예요. 원두를 내리는 도구(드립, 머신)에 따라 맛이 달라져요.
explain_en: It contrasts with '믹스커피' and '인스턴트커피' and means coffee brewed from ground beans. The coffee sold at cafes is usually this kind. The taste changes depending on how it is brewed, such as drip or machine.

examples.ko: 이 단어의 원뜻은 지금 쓰는 뜻과 많이 달라요.
examples.en: The original meaning of this word is very different from how it is used now.
It's easier to understand if you look up the original meaning in a dictionary.

examples.ko: 말이 변해서 원뜻이 잊힌 표현이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many expressions whose original meaning has been forgotten as the language changed.

examples.ko: 원뜻 그대로 쓰는 사람은 요즘 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Few people use it in its original sense these days.

examples.ko: 그 속담의 원뜻이 뭔지 정말 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm really curious what the original meaning of that proverb is.

examples.ko: 원뜻에서 조금 벗어나서 다른 뜻으로 쓰여요.
examples.en: It has drifted a bit from the original meaning and is used in another sense.

explain: 말이 시간이 지나며 바뀌었을 때, 처음 뜻과 지금 뜻을 비교하며 써요. 대화에서는 '원래 뜻', '본래 뜻'이라고도 많이 해요. 반대로 달라진 뜻은 '바뀐 뜻'이나 '비유적인 뜻'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when comparing a word's first meaning with its meaning now after the language has changed. In conversation people also say '원래 뜻' or '본래 뜻'. The changed meaning is called '바뀐 뜻' or '비유적인 뜻' (figurative meaning).

en: Year of the Monkey; person born in a Monkey year

examples.en: They say I'm curious because I'm a Monkey in the zodiac.
My older sister is a Monkey and I am a Dog.
I met a friend who was born in a Monkey year.
Are you a Monkey too, teacher? That's the same as me.

examples.ko: 원숭이띠 해는 열두 해마다 다시 돌아와요.
examples.en: A Monkey year comes around again every twelve years.

examples.ko: 올해 원숭이띠가 운이 좋다고 해서 기대돼요.
examples.en: They say Monkeys have good luck this year, so I'm looking forward to it.

explain: 십이지 동물로 태어난 해를 말해요. '무슨 띠예요?'에 '원숭이띠예요'라고 대답해요. '신년 운세'에서 띠별로 운을 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It names the zodiac animal of the year you were born. You answer '무슨 띠예요?' with '원숭이띠예요'. Zodiac signs are often used in New Year fortune readings.

examples.en: My monthly income is enough to cover living expenses.
My monthly income is unstable, so I'm worried.
I save about half of my monthly income.
The rent is too expensive compared to my monthly income.
If you add up the couple's monthly income, it's quite comfortable.

examples.ko: 월수입 대비 지출을 매달 적어 봐요.
examples.en: I write down my spending against my monthly income every month.

explain: '월급'은 회사에서 받는 돈이고, '월수입'은 장사나 부업 등을 포함해 한 달에 버는 돈 전체를 말할 수 있어요. 말할 때는 '한 달 수입'이라고도 해요. '월수입이 많다/적다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '월급' is the pay you receive from a company, while '월수입' can include everything you earn in a month, such as business or side jobs. In speech people also say '한 달 수입'. You say '월수입이 많다/적다'.

examples.ko: 월요일 아침마다 피곤한 걸 월요병이라고 해요.
examples.en: Feeling tired every Monday morning is called Monday blues.
The Monday blues start on Sunday night.
Because of the Monday blues, it's hard to get up in the morning.
I listen to music I like to beat the Monday blues.
Warm coffee is the best for the Monday blues.
Not only workers but students also get the Monday blues.

explain: 진짜 병이 아니라 주말이 끝나고 일이나 학교로 돌아가기 싫은 기분을 농담처럼 말하는 거예요. '월요병이 오다', '월요병에 걸리다'처럼 써요. 피곤하고 의욕이 없을 때 가볍게 말해요.
explain_en: It isn't a real illness but a joking way to describe not wanting to go back to work or school after the weekend. You say '월요병이 오다' or '월요병에 걸리다'. People use it lightly when they feel tired and unmotivated.

examples.ko: 위험물은 비행기에 가지고 탈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't bring hazardous materials onto a plane.

examples.ko: 위험물을 옮길 때는 특별히 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be especially careful when moving dangerous goods.

examples.ko: 이 창고에는 위험물이 많아서 불을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: There are many hazardous materials in this warehouse, so you must not use fire.

examples.ko: 위험물 표시가 있는 상자는 열지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't open boxes with a hazardous materials label.
I received safety training about hazardous materials.
It's classified as dangerous goods, so I can't send it by parcel.

explain: 공항, 택배, 공장의 안내문에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '위험한 물건'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요. '위험물 취급'처럼 뒤에 다른 말이 붙기도 해요.
explain_en: You often see this word in notices at airports, delivery services and factories. In everyday talk people often say '위험한 물건' instead. Other words can follow it, as in '위험물 취급' (handling hazardous materials).

examples.ko: ㄹ은 혀를 윗니 뒤에 대고 발음해요.
examples.en: You pronounce ㄹ with your tongue touching behind the upper teeth.
My upper tooth was loose, so I went to the dentist.

examples.ko: 웃을 때 윗니와 아랫니가 다 보여요.
examples.en: When I smile, both my upper and lower teeth show.
There is chili powder stuck in your upper teeth.
Try lightly biting your lower lip with your upper teeth.

examples.ko: 윗니는 아랫니보다 조금 더 앞으로 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The upper teeth stick out a little more than the lower teeth.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫니'예요. '윗'은 '위'가 아니라 '윗'으로 써서 [윈니]로 발음해요. 발음 수업이나 치과에서 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫니' (lower teeth). It is spelled with '윗' instead of '위' and pronounced [윈니]. You often hear it in pronunciation lessons and at the dentist.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추워서 윗도리를 하나 더 입었어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I put on another top.
I wore a white top and black pants.

examples.ko: 이 윗도리 사이즈가 저한테 좀 커요.
examples.en: This top is a bit big for me.
My top got wet, so I have to change.
This top has pockets, so it's convenient.
I bought the top and pants as a set.

explain: 바지나 치마와 짝으로 허리 위에 입는 옷을 말할 때 써요. 옷가게에서는 '상의'라는 말도 많이 해요. 편한 대화에서는 '윗도리'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used for clothes worn above the waist, paired with pants or skirts. In clothing stores you also hear '상의'. In casual conversation '윗도리' sounds natural.

examples.en: Please write your name on the top of the box.
The top of the desk has turned white with dust.
The top of the cake is covered in cream.

examples.ko: 윗면을 위로 해서 놓아야 깨지지 않아요.
examples.en: Put it with the top side facing up so it doesn't break.
The color of the top side is different from the bottom.
The wrapping paper on top has torn.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫면'이에요. 상자, 책상, 케이크처럼 모양이 있는 물건의 위쪽 면을 말할 때 써요. 방향만 말할 때는 그냥 '위쪽'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫면' (bottom side). It is used for the top surface of an object with a shape, such as a box, desk or cake. If you only mean direction, you simply say '위쪽'.

examples.en: The top and pants go well together.
Take off your top and hang it on the chair.
The top is too small, so I should buy a new one.
Dark colors are comfortable for tops.
I put the key in my top's pocket.
It rained and my top got stained.

explain: '윗도리'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 바지나 치마와 짝으로 말해요. '윗옷을 입다/벗다'처럼 써요. [위돋]으로 발음해요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '윗도리' and is paired with pants or skirts. You say '윗옷을 입다/벗다'. It is pronounced [위돋].

examples.en: My upper lip is swollen and hurts.
When it's cold, I put lip balm on my upper lip.
I have a habit of biting my upper lip when I worry.
You have a milk mark above your upper lip.
The upper lip is thin and the lower lip is full.
Try pressing your upper and lower lips together and then parting them.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫입술'이에요. '윗'을 쓰고 [윈닙쑬]로 발음해요. 'ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅍ' 소리를 낼 때 입술을 붙이는 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫입술' (lower lip). It is written with '윗' and pronounced [윈닙쑬]. It often appears in explanations of how to make the sounds ㅁ, ㅂ and ㅍ.

examples.en: Is it okay to make a U-turn up ahead?

examples.ko: 유턴 표지판을 못 봐서 그냥 지나쳤어요.
examples.en: I missed the U-turn sign and drove right past.
U-turns are prohibited on this road.
Make the U-turn at the next intersection.
I took a wrong road, so I came back with a U-turn.
There was nowhere to make a U-turn, so I kept going straight.

explain: 운전할 때 도로에서 반대 방향으로 도는 것을 말해요. 도로 표지판에 '유턴 금지'나 '유턴 허용'이 자주 보여요. 동사로는 '유턴하다'나 '유턴을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to turning around to the opposite direction on the road while driving. Road signs often show '유턴 금지' (no U-turn) or '유턴 허용'. As a verb you say '유턴하다' or '유턴을 하다'.

examples.en: Please make a U-turn at the next intersection.
I took a wrong road, so I made a hurried U-turn.
You can't make a U-turn here.
The taxi suddenly made a U-turn and I was startled.
I tried to make a U-turn, but there were too many cars.
Don't make a U-turn, go straight a bit more.

explain: 택시를 탔을 때 '여기서 유턴해 주세요'라고 자주 말해요. '유턴을 하다'로 나눠 써도 같아요. 길에서 반대 방향으로 돌 때만 쓰고, 마음이 바뀌어서 돌아가는 일에는 보통 '돌아가다'를 써요.
explain_en: When riding a taxi you often say '여기서 유턴해 주세요'. Splitting it as '유턴을 하다' means the same. It is for turning the car around on the road; for changing your mind and going back, people usually say '돌아가다'.

examples.en: My second cousin came to the wedding.
You have fewer chances to meet second cousins than first cousins.
My second cousin goes to the same university.
I think relatives up to second cousins are close relatives.

examples.ko: 아버지 쪽 육촌과는 거의 연락을 안 해요.
examples.en: I hardly keep in touch with my second cousins on my father's side.
I sent a wedding invitation to my second cousin.

explain: '육촌 형', '육촌 동생'처럼 뒤에 형·누나·동생을 붙여 불러요. 촌수는 숫자가 클수록 먼 친척이에요. 사촌보다 한 단계 더 먼 사이라서 자주 못 만나는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: You add words after it, as in '육촌 형' or '육촌 동생'. The bigger the 촌수 number, the more distant the relative. It is a step more distant than a first cousin, so people often don't meet them much.

examples.en: In autumn the ginkgo leaves turn yellow.
I walked stepping on the ginkgo leaves piled on the ground.
I made a bookmark out of a ginkgo leaf.
The color of the ginkgo leaves is really pretty.
A ginkgo leaf is shaped like a fan.
Sunlight shines on the yellow ginkgo leaves and it's dazzling.

explain: '은행'은 은행나무와 열매를 가리키기도 하고 'bank'와 소리가 같지만, 문맥으로 쉽게 구분돼요. 가을 단풍 이야기에서 '노란 은행잎'이 자주 나와요. [은행닙]으로 발음해요.
explain_en: '은행' can mean the ginkgo tree and its nut, and it sounds like 'bank', but the context makes it easy to tell. '노란 은행잎' (yellow ginkgo leaves) often comes up when talking about autumn colors. It is pronounced [은행닙].

examples.en: We sang loudly in the cheering section.
Our class's cheering section was the loudest.
I booked cheering section tickets in advance.
The fans who filled the cheering section stood up.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 응원석은 저쪽 파란 의자들이에요.
examples.en: Our team's cheering section is those blue seats over there.
To get to the cheering section, go up the stairs on the right.

explain: 야구장, 축구장, 운동회에서 응원하는 사람들이 모여 앉는 자리를 말해요. 일반 좌석과 구별해서 '응원석'이라고 해요. 응원가를 부르고 박수를 치는 분위기의 자리예요.
explain_en: This is the area at a baseball field, soccer stadium or sports day where supporters gather. It is named to distinguish it from regular seats. It's a spot where people sing cheer songs and clap together.

examples.en: I didn't feel well, so I went to the infirmary.
The infirmary nurse gave me medicine.

examples.ko: 의무실은 일 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The infirmary is at the end of the first-floor hallway.

examples.ko: 넘어져서 무릎을 다쳤으니 의무실로 가 보세요.
examples.en: You fell and hurt your knee, so go to the infirmary.

examples.ko: 죄송한데요, 이 건물 의무실이 어디에 있어요?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the infirmary in this building?

examples.ko: 의무실에서 열을 재 보니 조금 높았어요.
examples.en: I took my temperature at the infirmary and it was a little high.

explain: 회사, 군대, 공장처럼 사람이 많이 모인 곳에서 아픈 사람을 돌보는 방이에요. 학교에서는 보통 '보건실'이라고 해요. '의무실에 가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a room for looking after sick people in places with many people, such as companies, the military and factories. In schools it is usually called '보건실'. You say '의무실에 가다'.

en: have a doubt; doubt; be doubtful of

examples.ko: 이 문장이 맞는지 의심나서 선생님께 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I wasn't sure this sentence was right, so I asked the teacher.
Please mark the parts you have doubts about.
What that person said seems a little doubtful to me.
If you're unsure about the meaning, look it up in a dictionary.
I doubted it at first, but I believed it after hearing the explanation.

examples.ko: 의심날 때는 혼자 고민하지 말고 물어보세요.
examples.en: When you have doubts, don't worry alone, just ask.

explain: '의심나는 점', '의심나는 부분'처럼 확실하지 않아서 확인하고 싶은 것에 많이 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 '의심이 나는 대상'이라서 '문장이/말이 의심나요'처럼 말해요. '의심하다'는 사람이 어떤 것을 의심하는 행동에 써요.
explain_en: It is often used for things you aren't sure about and want to check, as in '의심나는 점' or '의심나는 부분'. The subject is the thing causing doubt, so you say '문장이/말이 의심나요'. '의심하다' is for a person actively suspecting something.

examples.en: You need willpower to go on a diet.
You can build willpower through practice.
He passed the exam through strong willpower.
There are times when willpower alone is not enough to hold out.

examples.ko: 의지력을 기르려고 매일 아침 일찍 일어나요.
examples.en: I get up early every morning to build willpower.
People with willpower see things through to the end.

explain: '의지력이 강하다/약하다'로 자주 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '끈기'가 있는데, 끈기는 포기하지 않고 계속하는 힘이고 의지력은 마음먹은 것을 해내려는 힘이에요. 그냥 '의지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: You often say '의지력이 강하다/약하다'. A similar word is '끈기', which is the staying power to keep going, while 의지력 is the strength of will to do what you decided. People also just say '의지'.

examples.ko: 이다음에 시간 되면 또 같이 와요.
examples.en: Let's come again together next time when we have time.
You can get off at the next stop.
Next is my turn to present.
Next time I'll make sure not to be late.
I'm worried about what comes next and I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 이다음 주에는 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like it will rain the week after this.

explain: '이다음에'는 '나중에, 훗날'처럼 막연한 앞날이나 다음 기회를 말할 때 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '다음에'나 '나중에'도 많이 써요. 순서를 말할 때는 '이다음 정류장'처럼 바로 뒤의 것을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '이다음에' is often used for a vague future or the next chance, like 'later' or 'someday'. In daily talk '다음에' and '나중에' are also common. For order, it points to the one right after this, as in '이다음 정류장' (the stop after this).

examples.en: A light drizzle has been falling since this morning.
It was only a drizzle, so I just walked without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 이슬비는 소리 없이 내려서 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: A drizzle falls without a sound, so you hardly notice it.
My clothes got a little wet in the drizzle.
I drank tea watching the drizzle outside the window.
On drizzly days I think of pajeon.

explain: 아주 가늘게 내리는 비예요. '가랑비', '보슬비', '안개비'도 가는 비를 가리키는 말이에요. 일기예보에서는 '약한 비'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is very fine, light rain. '가랑비', '보슬비' and '안개비' also refer to light rain. Weather forecasts often just say '약한 비' (light rain).

examples.en: Please take a toothpick from next to the cashier.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개로 이를 쑤시는 건 보기 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: Picking your teeth with a toothpick doesn't look nice.
We stick the rice cake on a toothpick and eat it.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개가 다 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of toothpicks, so I need to buy new ones.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개 한 통에 몇 개 들었어요?
examples.en: How many are in one box of toothpicks?

examples.ko: 이쑤시개는 입을 가리고 쓰는 게 예의예요.
examples.en: It is polite to cover your mouth when using a toothpick.

explain: 식당 계산대 옆에 놓여 있는 경우가 많아요. 이를 쑤시는 용도 말고도 과일이나 떡을 집어 먹는 데도 써요. '이'(teeth)와 '쑤시다'(poke)가 합쳐진 말이라서 소리 나는 대로 [이쑤시개]라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often left next to the cashier in restaurants. Besides cleaning teeth, it's also used to pick up fruit or rice cakes. It combines '이' (teeth) and '쑤시다' (to poke) and is pronounced [이쑤시개].

examples.ko: 이번 여행이 두고두고 이야깃거리가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This trip will probably be something to talk about for a long time.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 자리라서 이야깃거리를 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's our first meeting, so it's hard to find things to talk about.
Celebrity news is always a good topic.
What else can we talk about besides the weather?

examples.ko: 그 영화가 요즘 친구들 사이에서 이야깃거리로 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: That movie has become a topic among friends lately.

examples.ko: 모임에서 나눌 이야깃거리 좀 생각해 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you thought of some topics to talk about at the gathering?

explain: '볼거리', '먹을거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙어서 이야기할 만한 재료라는 느낌이에요. 줄여서 '얘깃거리'라고도 해요. 비슷한 말로 '화젯거리'가 있어요.
explain_en: Like '볼거리' and '먹을거리', the '-거리' ending gives the feel of material worth talking about. It is shortened to '얘깃거리' in speech. A similar word is '화젯거리'.

examples.en: I took the last runner's spot in the relay race at the sports day.
Teamwork is really important in a relay race.
Our class came first in the relay race.
I fell while practicing for the relay race.
I was picked as a relay runner, so I'm nervous.
When the relay race started, the cheering got louder.

explain: 학교 운동회에서 가장 인기 있는 종목 중 하나예요. '릴레이'라는 외래어도 쓰고, 운동 경기에서는 '계주'라고도 해요. '이어달리기를 하다', '이어달리기에 나가다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is one of the most popular events at school sports days. The loanword '릴레이' is also used, and in athletics the term '계주' is common. You say '이어달리기를 하다' or '이어달리기에 나가다'.

examples.en: The interest rate differs a little from bank to bank.
The interest rate can change every month.
I compared loan interest rates and then decided.
I borrowed money at a 3 percent annual interest rate.

examples.ko: 이자율에 따라 갚을 돈이 크게 달라져요.
examples.en: The amount you pay back varies greatly depending on the interest rate.
Loans feel like a burden these days because of interest rates.

explain: 뉴스나 은행에서는 '이율', '금리'라는 말도 많이 써요. '이자율이 오르다/내리다/높다/낮다'처럼 말해요. 예금과 대출 모두에 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: In the news and at banks, '이율' and '금리' are also common. You say '이자율이 오르다/내리다/높다/낮다'. It applies to both savings and loans.

examples.ko: 이종사촌 동생이 우리 집에 놀러 왔어요.
examples.en: My younger cousin on my mother's sister's side came to visit.

examples.ko: 저는 이종사촌과 어릴 때부터 가깝게 지냈어요.
examples.en: I've been close with my maternal-aunt cousin since childhood.

examples.ko: 제 이종사촌은 나이가 비슷해서 친구 같아요.
examples.en: My cousin is about my age, so we're like friends.
I took lots of photos at my cousin's wedding.
I asked for my cousin's address to send a gift.

examples.ko: 이종사촌이 서울로 이사 와서 자주 만나요.
examples.en: My cousin moved to Seoul, so we meet often.

explain: 엄마의 자매(이모)의 자녀를 말해요. 엄마 쪽이라도 외삼촌의 자녀는 '외사촌'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 일상에서는 그냥 '사촌'이라고만 부르는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It means the child of your mother's sister (이모). Even on your mother's side, the child of your mother's brother is called '외사촌', which is different. In daily life people often just say '사촌'.

examples.ko: 아이가 이해력이 빨라서 한 번만 설명해도 알아요.
examples.en: The child understands quickly, so one explanation is enough.

examples.ko: 이해력을 높이려면 책을 많이 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To improve comprehension you need to read lots of books.
Comprehension is really important in learning a foreign language.

examples.ko: 이해력에 비해 말하기 실력이 아직 낮아요.
examples.en: My speaking skill is still low compared to my comprehension.

examples.ko: 아이의 이해력 수준에 맞는 책을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose a book that matches the child's level of comprehension.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말도 잘하고 이해력도 좋아요.
examples.en: That person speaks well and also understands things well.

explain: '이해력이 빠르다/느리다/좋다/부족하다'처럼 말해요. 글을 읽고 이해하는 힘은 '독해력'이라고 해서 따로 있어요. 이해력은 말, 설명, 상황까지 넓게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: You say '이해력이 빠르다/느리다/좋다/부족하다'. The ability to read and understand text has its own word, '독해력'. 이해력 is broader and covers speech, explanations and situations.

examples.ko: 인스턴트식품을 너무 자주 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Eating instant food too often is bad for your health.
Instant food is convenient, but a lot of it is salty.
When I'm busy, I get by on instant food.

examples.ko: 인스턴트식품 대신 직접 요리해 먹기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to cook for myself instead of eating instant food.
The fridge is full of instant food.
What kinds of things count as instant food?

explain: 라면, 즉석밥, 냉동식품처럼 간단히 조리해서 먹는 음식을 말해요. '즉석식품'이라는 말도 비슷하게 써요. 건강 이야기에서는 조금 부정적인 느낌으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It covers food that is simple to prepare, like ramen, instant rice and frozen food. '즉석식품' is a similar term. In talk about health it often carries a slightly negative feel.

examples.en: I eat injeolmi coated generously with soybean powder.
Injeolmi is chewy and nutty, so I eat it often.
My grandmother made injeolmi for me herself.
I bought a pack of injeolmi at the rice cake shop.
Shaved ice made with injeolmi is popular.

examples.ko: 시장에서 인절미가 갓 나와서 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: Fresh injeolmi had just come out at the market, so I bought one.

explain: 찹쌀로 만든 떡에 콩가루를 묻힌 대표적인 한국 떡이에요. 콩가루는 '콩고물'이라고도 해요. 요즘은 '인절미 맛' 라떼나 아이스크림처럼 맛 이름으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a classic Korean rice cake made from glutinous rice and coated in soybean powder. The powder is also called '콩고물'. These days the name is also used as a flavor, as in injeolmi latte or ice cream.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 일과표를 직접 짜 봤어요.
examples.en: I made my own daily schedule during the vacation.
Moving by my daily schedule makes time pass well.

examples.ko: 일과표에는 점심시간이 한 시간으로 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The daily schedule says lunch is one hour.

examples.ko: 일과표가 너무 빡빡해서 쉴 틈이 없어요.
examples.en: The daily schedule is so tight that there's no time to rest.

examples.ko: 친구에게 내 일과표 좀 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my friend my daily schedule.
I put exercise time in my daily schedule too.

explain: 하루에 할 일을 시간 순서대로 적은 표예요. 학교 수업을 적은 표는 '시간표'라고 해서 달라요. 캠프나 훈련처럼 하루 일정이 정해진 곳에서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It's a chart of what you will do during the day in time order. A chart of school classes is called '시간표', which is different. It's also commonly used for camps and training programs with a fixed daily routine.
